status: Five design options for Tamsin Station's spacedock, for the owner to choose between (openspec/changes/spacedock). Read by docs/mockups/spacedock.html only; the engine reads the chosen option once the change is applied.
_doc: Station frame: metres, origin at the station's centre, +y the station's north, +z the way the main doors face. Ships' frames as layout.json: +x port, +y up, +z the bow. Angles in degrees; bearings round +y from +z toward +x. Colours sRGB 0-1.

sky._doc: The view at the station, in its own frame: the star high behind the approach, Tamsin below and beyond (17.5 degrees in radius at 3.33 radii, patrol-mission design 2). Orrin and Cinder are points of light from here (under 0.02 degrees).

traffic._doc: The approach and the bay's speed limits. The doors open when traffic control clears the ship and the bow is inside the approach corridor (doors_open_s); inside the doors the bay limit holds until the berth, where flight-and-navigation 10's docking corridor (2 m/s inside 100 m, 0.5 m/s inside 10 m, 0.2 m/s at contact) takes over.

fleet._doc: The ships at the berths: the Tern's liveries and the Osprey (assets/models/exteriors), and the Federation concepts (data/ships/federation-concepts). A docked ship is drawn at its middle level of detail in the engine.

A.name: Bastion
A.brief: A domed cap 1.8 km across on a ringed tower 2 km tall. Four doors in the cap's rim open into one round hall 1.7 km across and 140 m high, with the berths set round a central core like the spokes of a wheel.

berths._doc: [bearing, ship, radius of the ship's middle]: an outer ring and an inner ring, bows toward the core.

B.name: Wheel
B.brief: A habitat wheel 1.75 km across on six spokes round a hub drum 540 m across. The hub's front doors open along the axis into a cylindrical hangar where ships berth all round the curved wall, overhead too.

berths._slots: [row, angle round the axis from the bottom, ship]

C.name: Drydock
C.brief: A long armoured hall 1.7 km long with a command tower and a habitat block at its stern. One pair of doors at the bow opens onto a fairway 400 m wide, with six berths down each wall where ships lie bow out, ready to leave.

berths._slots: [wall (-1 starboard, +1 port, as the ships lie bow out), z, ship]

D.name: Hollow
D.brief: A captured nickel-iron asteroid 2.2 km long, hollowed into a cavern 1.3 km deep. An armoured gate in its face opens into the rock; inside, the berths stand on a built deck down both sides, lit galleries cut into the walls.

E.name: O'Neill Pair
E.brief: Two hollow O'Neill cylinders 6.4 km long and 1.8 km across, side by side and turning opposite ways, their axes on the star. Inside each, three valleys of farmland, rivers and towns curve up overhead between three long windows, under a patchy cloud layer; three mirrors bloom open from the far end like petals and throw the star in through the windows. Ships enter on the axis, through a non-rotating port at the sunward dome of one cylinder, into an enclosed hall.
E._owner: 2026-10-14: "what about an oneil cylinder space station? can you make some textures for that? a giant cylinder? wiht a big space station attached at one end. theres usually two of them to counter balance rotational effects"; "What oneil cylinders are hollowed cylinders. Didn't you research what they looked like and how they work?"; "Also notice how the solar panels open up on one side they are blooming slightly like aflower"; "The ends are round and should have an opening for ships to enter"
E._sun: The star on the cylinders' axes (Wikipedia, O'Neill cylinder: each cylinder's axis points at the sun), in the station's frame; A-D keep sky.sun_dir.

port._doc: Our own design: a non-rotating, round, recessed collar on the axis at the sunward dome of cylinder 0 (the axis is the only place nearly still, with no spin gravity): a lit ring mouth of radius hole_radius_m, its throat recess_m deep, rings of light on the dome leading in, the hall sunk behind it in the dome's hub.

textures._doc: Two layers (owner, 2026-10-14: "we should have 2 layers of texture, detail layer, and the big albiedo color map, and maybe normal maps on the details"): macro maps wrapped once (the outside round a cylinder, the land over a stripe, the clouds round their layer, a dome) multiplied by tiled detail layers, the hull's with its normal map, the detail fading out between fade_m. Made in Material Maker (tools/materials/ptex/oneill_*.ptex), packaged by tools/materials/oneill_atlases.py.
